assertions.description: WebTransport.prototype.getStats is a function in this secure context.
getStats() returns a Promise synchronously, even on a transport that is still connecting.
assertions.test: (() => { const wt = new WebTransport('https://getstats-probe.invalid/'); wt.ready.catch(() => {}); wt.closed.catch(() => {}); const p = wt.getStats(); p.catch(() => {}); return p instanceof Promise; })()

assertions.description: getStats() called while the connection is still connecting waits, then rejects with InvalidStateError when the handshake fails.
assertions.test: (async () => { const wt = new WebTransport('https://getstats-probe.invalid/'); wt.closed.catch(() => {}); const p = wt.getStats(); try { await wt.ready; return false; } catch {} try { await p; return false; } catch (e) { return e instanceof DOMException && e.name === 'InvalidStateError'; } })()

assertions.description: getStats() on a WebTransport whose connection has failed rejects with InvalidStateError.
assertions.test: (async () => { const wt = new WebTransport('https://getstats-probe.invalid/'); wt.closed.catch(() => {}); try { await wt.ready; return false; } catch {} try { await wt.getStats(); return false; } catch (e) { return e instanceof DOMException && e.name === 'InvalidStateError'; } })()

assertions.description: getStats() is also exposed on WebTransport in a dedicated worker and rejects with InvalidStateError for a failed connection there.
assertions.test: (async () => { const src = "onmessage = async () => { try { const wt = new WebTransport('https://getstats-probe.invalid/'); wt.closed.catch(() => {}); if (typeof wt.getStats !== 'function') { postMessage('missing'); return; } try { await wt.getStats(); postMessage('resolved'); } catch (e) { postMessage(e.name); } } catch (e) { postMessage('threw ' + e.name); } };"; const url = URL.createObjectURL(new Blob([src], { type: 'text/javascript' })); const w = new Worker(url); const r = await new Promise((res) => { w.onmessage = (e) => res(e.data); w.onerror = () => res('error'); w.postMessage(0); setTimeout(() => res('timeout'), 5000); }); w.terminate(); URL.revokeObjectURL(url); return r === 'InvalidStateError'; })()

assertions.description: Setting datagrams.incomingMaxAge to 0 stores null, and a positive value reads back unchanged; this knob controls datagrams.expiredIncoming.
assertions.test: (() => { const wt = new WebTransport('https://getstats-probe.invalid/'); wt.ready.catch(() => {}); wt.closed.catch(() => {}); const d = wt.datagrams; d.incomingMaxAge = 40; const a = d.incomingMaxAge; d.incomingMaxAge = 0; return a === 40 && d.incomingMaxAge === null; })()

assertions.description: On an established session, getStats() resolves with a datagrams object of non-negative counters and an estimatedSendRate that is null or a number of bits per second; RTT members, when present, are milliseconds as numbers.
assertions.test: Needs a live HTTP/3 WebTransport server, which this site cannot host. Connect from the stats field inspector page to a public or local echo server and check the per-member table.

assertions.description: After the session closes, getStats() still resolves with the most recent stats available instead of rejecting.
assertions.test: Needs an established session to close. Run experiment 7 on the closed and failed connections page against an echo server.
